## 1. What was read

**800 research articles** from 33 of the 33 journals on the roster.

A further **127** records (14% of the 927 this month's harvest returned) carry no abstract and are not research: news, correspondence, editor highlights and obituaries. PubMed types them `Journal Article` and nothing else, so the publication-type filter cannot see them — across the whole index they are 22.7% of it and 35% of `general`, and 3,801 of them are JAMA. !!! warning "Volume swing against the median month: cancer -28%"
    Check the source before reading anything into this. Two benign causes account for most of these. `bioinfo` every January carries the Nucleic Acids Research database issue and runs high. And several journals simply deposit nothing in some months: across the 44 months read, 4 of 33 journals are absent from at least one, worst being *Nat Mach Intell* (20 months missing, 81 papers in total) and *Bioinformatics* (4 months missing, 2,905 papers in total). Every journal on the roster contributed this month. Queried directly, PubMed returns zero for those journal-months too — the holes are in the source, reproduced exactly by re-running the harvest. So a swing here is not evidence that a field went quiet, and is not usually evidence that the pipeline broke either.

Largest contributors: Bioinformatics 109, Nature 102, Nucleic Acids Res 89, Science 77, Lancet 43, JAMA 38.

## 3. The evidence that moved it

**Hallucination detection lands in *Nature*.** [38898292](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38898292/): detecting
hallucinations in large language models using semantic entropy. The December
2025 briefing calls auditing a generative model's own output — rather than its
training or its benchmarks — "a new category". It is in *Nature* eighteen months
earlier. This is the fifth first-appearance claim in this corpus to move earlier
on extension, and at this point the individual corrections matter less than the
rule: **first appearance is a property of the window.**

**Two acetylcholine papers, same journal, same month.** [38744292](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38744292/) and
[38744291](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38744291/) (*Immunity*): tuft-cell acetylcholine released into the gut lumen
to promote anti-helminth immunity, and tuft-cell-derived acetylcholine driving
epithelial chloride secretion and helminth clearance. With [38772371](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38772371/)
(*Cell*) — innervation of nociceptor neurons in the spleen promoting
germinal-centre responses — June 2024 has nerves controlling a lymphoid organ and
a named neurotransmitter doing immune work, in the corpus's top venues, in one
month.

## 4. Refutations

### (a) Landing on a tracked thread

Nineteen of this month's refutations land on a tracked thread other than
`method-credibility`. Four groups of them carry the month.

**The lead second-generation checkpoint is read out against a control twice, and
adds nothing either time.** [38723227](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38723227/)
(*JCO*) — RELATIVITY-060 missed its primary endpoint: adding relatlimab
(anti-LAG-3) to nivolumab plus chemotherapy in LAG-3-expressing gastric and
gastro-oesophageal junction cancer gave a numerically worse response rate (48%
against 61%), worse progression-free survival (HR 1.41) and more grade 3–4
toxicity than nivolumab plus chemotherapy alone — in a biomarker-selected
population, which is the condition under which this class was supposed to work.
[38689060](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38689060/) (*Nat Med*) — in resectable
non-small-cell lung cancer, neoadjuvant nivolumab with relatlimab gave a major
pathological response of 30% against 27% for nivolumab alone, with complete
resection in 90% against 100%. `next-gen-checkpoints` has been carrying registry
activity as its evidence — whether a nominated target reached a phase 1 — and this
is what the readouts look like when they arrive.

**The myeloid checkpoint destroys the therapy it was meant to complement.**
[38750365](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38750365/) (*Nature*) — combining
anti-CD47 antibodies with adoptive T-cell therapy abrogated the benefit outright:
macrophages cleared the CAR and TCR T cells fast enough that the antibody worked
as a safety switch, and only a CD47 variant invisible to the antibody rescued the
combination. It refutes `next-gen-checkpoints` and `cell-therapy` at once, and it
is a combination failure neither thread could have anticipated from its own cards.

**Four cards say the suppressive population was doing something.**
[38788719](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38788719/) (*Cancer Cell*) — TREM2, the
canonical immunosuppressive myeloid target being blocked in peripheral cancers, is
protective in glioblastoma: genetic or pharmacological deficiency accelerated
progression, and overexpression impeded growth and synergised with anti-PD-1.
[38759656](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38759656/) (*Cancer Cell*) — effective
immunotherapy in two murine models required a late-stage activated M1-like
macrophage population recruited via CCR5 by therapy-induced CD8 T cells, and the
authors warn explicitly that broad macrophage-targeting combinations would remove
it. [38692280](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38692280/) (*Immunity*) — depleting
visceral-adipose Treg cells, or Treg-derived oncostatin-M, or its receptor on
stromal cells, strongly impaired insulin sensitivity, on an axis the authors
report as conserved in humans. And
[38811815](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38811815/) (*Nat Immunol*) — bone-marrow
neutrophils polarised with IL-4 and G-CSF secrete growth factors and drive optic
nerve and spinal cord axon regeneration, which is the same argument from the other
side: the therapeutic move is reprogramming, not depletion.

**A molecular residual-disease endpoint gives the wrong answer inside a randomised
trial.** [38452207](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38452207/) (*Blood*) —
GRAAPH-2014 de-escalated consolidation in Philadelphia-positive ALL using
BCR::ABL1 molecular response as the endpoint. The omission arm met non-inferiority
for major molecular response, 77.2% against 71.1%, and then relapsed at 31.3% at
four years against 13.2%; the DSMB halted the randomisation. Beside it
[38142939](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38142939/) (*Ann Oncol*) has ctDNA in
high-grade osteosarcoma refining a risk score and never guiding therapy, with the
assay's sensitivity at surgery and end of treatment too low to follow disease at
all. `ctdna-mrd` closes −2 with nothing on the other side.

    This section read, in full: "Nothing this month lands a refutation on a
    tracked thread, and that is worth recording rather than padding. The month's
    refutations are all methodological." Nineteen refutations land on a tracked
    thread other than `method-credibility`, including two randomised trials of the
    field's lead second-generation checkpoint. June 2024 had been carded from
    titles; none of the trial results above announces its outcome in its title —
    "Neoadjuvant nivolumab with or without relatlimab", "First-Line Nivolumab and

    benchmarks and concluded the biology was quiet. On
    `next-gen-checkpoints` it is in fact the joint-largest month in the corpus to
    that point — seven cards, tying November 2023 — and four of those seven
    refute.

### (b) Method credibility

[38886757](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38886757/) (*Genome Biol*): beyond benchmarking, towards predictive models
of dataset-specific pipeline performance. The claim is that a benchmark ranking
does not transfer between datasets — which, if true, undercuts the evidentiary
value of the benchmark papers that fill this journal every month, including
[37537502](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/37537502/) in the same month systematically benchmarking single-cell ATAC
protocols.

[38940140](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38940140/): BioCoder, a benchmark for bioinformatics code generation with
LLMs. The corpus's July 2026 briefing treats the arrival of benchmarks as the
maturity signal for the agentic thread. Here the benchmark arrives alongside the
capability rather than after it, which weakens benchmarks-as-maturity-signal as
a general reading.
